chunks: 10 - Salih ibn Isa ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rowyani narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ijli narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated to me, from his father, from Aban the client of Zayd ibn Ali, from Asim ibn Bahdala, he said:

Shurayh the Judge said to me: I bought a house for eighty gold coins, I wrote a document and had just witnesses testify. This reached Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), so he sent his servant Qanbar to me and I came to him. When I entered upon him, he said: O Shurayh, you bought a house, you wrote a document, you had witnesses testify, and you weighed out money? I said: Yes.

He said: O Shurayh, fear God, for indeed one will come to you who will not look at your document nor ask for your evidence, until he takes you out of your house departing and delivers you wholly to your grave. So make sure you did not buy this house from other than its rightful owner and that you did not pay with unlawful money, or else you will have lost both abodes together: this world and the Hereafter.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: O Shurayh, if you had come to me when you bought this house, I would have written you a document on this template, and you would not have bought it even for two silver coins. I said: What would you have written, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: I would have written this document for you:

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what was purchased by a lowly slave from a mortal urged to depart. He bought from him a house in the Abode of Vanity, from the side of the mortals to the garrison of the perished. This house has four boundaries: the first ends at the causes of destruction, the second at the causes of impairment, the third at the causes of calamity, and the fourth at ruinous desire and Satan the deceiver, and therein opens the door of this house. This deceived one, beguiled by wishful thinking, purchased from the one pursued by death the entirety of this house, by leaving the honour of contentment and entering the humiliation of worldly pursuit. Whatever befalls this buyer in what he bought, it is upon the One who wears out the bodies of kings and seizes the souls of tyrants like Khosrow, Caesar, Tubba, and Himyar, and all who amassed wealth upon wealth and increased it, who built and raised high structures, furnished and decorated them, and hoarded them claiming it was for their children -- dispatching them all to the station of accounting for the final judgment, and there the followers of falsehood were at total loss.

This is witnessed by the intellect when it emerges from the captivity of desires and looks with the eye of transience upon the people of this world, and hears the caller of asceticism proclaiming in its courtyards: How clear is the truth for one with eyes! Indeed departure is one of two days. Take provisions from righteous deeds and draw your hopes near to the reality of death, for the journey and the departure have drawn near.

key_terms.القنوع: Contentment with modest means -- a core virtue in Islamic ethics (qana'a)
key_terms.المبطلون: The followers of falsehood -- Quranic term (40:78) for those who pursue vanity over truth
key_terms.دار الغرور: Abode of Vanity/Delusion -- a metaphor for the transient, deceptive nature of worldly life
key_terms.شاخصا: Departing -- used here to describe the soul leaving the body at death

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to the judge Shurayh about buying a house?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) admonished Shurayh the Judge of Kufa after he bought a luxurious house for eighty dinars. Ali warned him that the angel of death will not care about property deeds or witnesses, and that buying from unlawful sources would mean losing both this world and the Hereafter. He then dictated a symbolic deed of sale portraying all worldly property as a transaction between a lowly slave and a departing mortal in the 'Abode of Vanity' -- bounded by destruction, disease, calamity, and satanic temptation. The document ends with a call to prepare for the inevitable journey through righteous deeds. This teaching was delivered during Ali's caliphate in Kufa (c. 35-40 AH), where Shurayh served as the chief judge.
